sourceTitle: Why the Middle Class Is Disappearing
title: The Middle Class Is Quietly Disappearing
hook: The middle class share of income, then and now.
question: Do you still count as middle class?

scenes.narration: The American middle class never really vanished. Instead, it got quietly squeezed, year after year, for about five decades.
Back in nineteen seventy-one, sixty-one percent of US adults counted as middle class. Today that share is down to roughly half.

shots.kicker: Share of US adults, middle class
shots.sub: it didn't vanish — it got squeezed

scenes.narration: Even pinning down what counts as middle class has become surprisingly slippery.
The reason is that most of the income gains piled up at the very top.
And the dream of doing better than your parents is fading. The odds a child out-earns them are now close to a coin flip.
Economists call that steadily collapsing economic mobility.
So, by the numbers, do you still count as middle class?
